sentences.label: Lowering the risk
sentences.text: These add up independently, and these lower the risk: being a woman takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 22% to about 3% and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 11%; a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily, from about 27% at 118 to about 18% at 175 beats per minute; and through this sum alone typical angina lowers it to about 2%, non-anginal chest pain to about 5% and atypical angina to about 11% (chest pain type also acts through the blood pressure step, below).

sentences.label: Raising the risk
sentences.text: Each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy adds about the same, from about 22% at 0 to about 88% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher; a flat rather than upsloping ST segment raises it to about 67%, higher cholesterol raises it steadily from about 14% at 193 mg/dL to about 37% at 308 mg/dL, and chest pain brought on by exercise raises it to about 33%.

Through this sum alone, higher resting blood pressure raises it steadily, from about 14% at 110 mm Hg to about 35% at 155 mm Hg, older age raises it steadily, from about 19% at 42 to about 24% at 66 years, and a reversible defect on the thallium scan raises it to about 35%; all three also act through the parts below.

sentences.label: Rare results
sentences.text: Some rarer results also count (the model has little data on this, n = 2 to 17): through this sum alone a thallium result coded 4 raises the risk to about 83% and a fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers it to about 11%, and a downsloping ST segment raises it to about 27%.

This part reads ST depression on exercise, the thallium scan and the resting ECG, and acts on 116 of 242 training patients, 77 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 89% without it and about 96% with it.
Through it, more ST depression adds to the predicted risk only once it rises above about 0.9 mm, rising in an uneven way: for a typical patient from about 22% at 0 mm to about 48% at 2.8 mm.

ST depression counts more with a reversible defect on the thallium scan (from about 36% to about 80%, against about 22% to about 48% otherwise) and with a normal resting ECG (from about 22% to about 48%, against about 22% to about 34% otherwise), in an uneven way.
A reversible defect on the thallium scan also raises the risk more with a normal resting ECG, from about 22% to about 47% against about 22% to about 36% otherwise.

This part reads that signal together with resting blood pressure and chest pain type, and barely changes the predictions: for the typical patient it acts on, atypical angina raises the predicted risk through it from about 69% to about 70%, and non-anginal chest pain leaves it at about 69%.
This part acts on 85 of 242 training patients, 37 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 28% without it and about 30% with it.

parts.original_hypothesis: Root: p = sigmoid(z), z = -0.504 + LINEAR CORE + 0.143*ischaemia_gate + 0.170*bp_offset_gate + 0.143*age_gate_without_ischaemia. LINEAR CORE (19 direct input->output edges, z-scored inputs): ca +1.480, sex:0 -1.072, slope:1 -0.855, chol +0.546, cp:1 -0.493, trestbps +0.480, cp:3 -0.440, exang:1 +0.431, thal:3 -0.410, thal:6 -0.384, cp:4 +0.377, slope:3 -0.366, fbs:0 +0.278, thalach -0.207, thal:4 +0.183, slope:2 +0.153, exang:0 +0.149, age +0.117, thal:7 -0.077. Four inputs are unconnected (sex:1, fbs:1, restecg:1, restecg:2; zero-effect entries of this root). Oldpeak, restecg:0 and cp:2 have no direct edge and act only through the chain. COMPOSITION: serial and additive. The three children form a chain, each read out additively into z: ischaemia_gate (oldpeak, normal resting ECG, reversible defect) feeds bp_offset_gate (the ischaemia score minus a resting-BP offset), which in turn switches off age_gate_without_ischaemia (an extra age term for patients without ischaemia evidence). The chain therefore raises risk with ST depression, more steeply where resting BP is low, and adds a small age term where the chain is quiet. Identity nodes identity_290 and identity_1987 carry the chain links (204 -> 290, 290 -> 1987) so that each gate is its own leaf. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): full model AUC 0.9418, acc 0.872 (compute_performance). Linear core alone AUC 0.934; logit SD 3.14 (core) vs 0.67 (chain). Removing the whole chain (node 204 with downstream) gives 0.934; readout-only ablations: ischaemia 0.940, BP 0.939, age 0.941. Treating all three ReLUs as identities gives 0.936; one least-squares linear fit of the chain on its seven inputs gives 0.937 (R2 0.84); an L2 logistic regression on all 26 inputs gives 0.936. Mean |SHAP| (train, all 242): ca 0.144, sex:0 0.110, slope:1 0.100, thal:3 0.048, exang:1 0.047, chol 0.045, cp:4 0.044, cp:3 0.044. Interpretation: close to logistic regression plus one ischaemia correction: ST depression raises risk only above a threshold set by a normal resting ECG and a reversible defect, more so when resting BP is low; age gets a small extra weight when there is no such evidence. Counter-directional signs reported, not explained: restecg:0 positive in the ischaemia gate, trestbps negative in the BP gate, fbs:0 +0.28 directly. Same design as the 10-seed heart-s5 record (generation 37, key 9330: ischaemia gate -> resting-BP gate -> age term), here with three hidden nodes instead of six.

parts.name: ischaemia_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Ischaemia-evidence gate (raises risk). 204 = ReLU(0.247 + 2.593*oldpeak + 0.871*restecg:0 + 1.145*thal:7). Hypothesis: a one-sided ST-depression score that opens above an oldpeak threshold set by two flags (always open with a normal resting ECG and a reversible thallium defect; above z-oldpeak -0.09 with a normal ECG only, -0.33 with a defect only, +0.58 with neither), and then raises the logit with oldpeak, directly (0.143 per unit) and through the blood-pressure gate (a further 0.183 per unit while that gate is open). EVIDENCE (train, n=242): active for 48% (100% of the 44 patients with both flags, 20% of the 75 with neither); corr with oldpeak 0.88; disease rate 66% when active vs 24% when inactive. Mean |sensitivity| oldpeak 1.24 > thal:7 0.55 > restecg:0 0.42. This is the main nonlinear effect: removing it with its downstream effects lowers train AUC 0.942 -> 0.934 (to the linear-core level); an affine replacement recovers 0.938. Supported. Oldpeak and restecg:0 have no direct edge; they act only here. The positive restecg:0 weight (normal ECG raises the score) is counter-intuitive and is reported, not explained.

parts.name: bp_offset_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Blood-pressure offset gate on the ischaemia score (raises risk). 290 = ReLU(-0.495 + 1.079*ischaemia_gate - 0.815*trestbps + 0.176*cp:2 + 0.016*cp:3). Hypothesis: passes the ischaemia score on, minus an offset that grows with resting blood pressure; it adds 0.170 per unit to the logit and switches off the age gate. With the ischaemia gate closed it still opens for low resting blood pressure, so within this gate lower resting BP raises risk (0.170*0.815 = 0.139 per SD), partly offsetting trestbps's direct +0.48 edge. cp:2 (atypical angina) nudges it open; cp:3's weight 0.016 is negligible. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): active for 58% (83% with the ischaemia gate open, 35% without); with the ischaemia gate open, active for 100%, 87% and 59% of the low, middle and high resting-BP groups. Disease rate 51% when active vs 35% when inactive. Mean |sensitivity| ischaemia score 0.58 > trestbps 0.45 > cp:2 0.10 > cp:3 0.01. Readout ablation lowers train AUC 0.942 -> 0.939; an affine replacement fits it well (R2 0.97, AUC 0.941), so its nonlinearity matters little. Supported, small. The negative BP term inside a risk-raising gate is reported, not explained.

parts.name: age_gate_without_ischaemia
parts.original_hypothesis: Age gate without ischaemia evidence (raises risk with age, small). 1987 = ReLU(0.203 + 0.875*age - 1.589*bp_offset_gate), read out +0.143. Hypothesis: an extra age term (0.125 per SD of age, on top of age's direct +0.117) that acts only while the BP gate is closed or nearly closed, i.e. for patients without much ischaemia evidence; any opening of the BP gate cancels it (each unit of the BP gate removes 0.227 from the logit through this node until it closes). EVIDENCE (train, n=242): active for 35% (65% when the BP gate is closed, rising with age: 0%, 80%, 100% of the youngest, middle and oldest groups; 14% when the BP gate is open). Disease rate barely differs (43% vs 45%). Mean |sensitivity| BP gate 0.35, age 0.31. Removing it lowers train AUC only 0.942 -> 0.941. Supported, near-negligible.

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

ann_32.text: This part acts on 116 of 242 training patients (48%).
For a typical patient it acts on, it raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 89% without this part to about 96% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 77 of these 116 patients had heart disease.

A higher ST depression on exercise clearly raises the predicted risk of heart disease, and even more so if the thallium scan shows a reversible defect (in an uneven way for patients with a reversible defect on the thallium scan): for a typical patient, ST depression on exercise going from 0.0 mm to 2.8 mm moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 36% to about 80% if the thallium scan shows a reversible defect, and from about 22% to about 48% if thallium stress test result is something other than a reversible defect on the thallium scan.

Other effects: a higher ST depression on exercise raises it in an uneven way; ST depression on exercise past about 0.9 mm raises it in an uneven way; ST depression on exercise depending on resting ECG raises it in an uneven way; thallium stress test result depending on resting ECG raises it; a reversible defect on the thallium scan (rather than any other thallium stress test result) raises it (on the training data only).
Smaller effects, each changing the predicted value only slightly: any other resting ECG (rather than a normal resting ECG) lowers it (on the training data only).

In the training data, 37 of these 85 patients had heart disease.

Through this part, age only slightly adds to the predicted risk of heart disease once it rises above about 53 years (between 53 and 66 years for different patients): for a typical such patient, going from 29 years to 68 years moves it from about 20% to about 24% (on the training data only).

summary.text: The model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, it goes from about 22% at 0 vessels to about 88% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 67%) than if the ST segment slopes up at peak exercise (about 22%) (on the training data only).

The model treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the predicted risk of heart disease in an uneven way: for a typical patient, it goes from about 22% at 0.0 mm to about 48% at 2.8 mm (on the training data only).

Through one part of the model, ST depression on exercise only adds to the predicted risk of heart disease once it rises above about 0.9 mm: for a typical such patient, going from 0.0 mm to 3.5 mm moves it from about 22% to about 46%; across patients the change happens in an uneven way (on the training data only).

The model gives a clearly higher predicted risk of heart disease if the thallium scan shows a reversible defect than if thallium stress test result is something other than a reversible defect on the thallium scan, and even more so if the resting ECG is normal: for a typical patient, going from thallium stress test result other than a reversible defect on the thallium scan to a reversible defect on the thallium scan moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 22% to about 47% if the resting ECG is normal, and from about 22% to about 36% if resting ECG is something other than a normal resting ECG.
